title: The Oxen and the Axletrees
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A pair of Oxen were drawing a heavily loaded waggon along the highway, and, as they tugged and strained at the yoke, the Axletrees creaked and groaned terribly. This was too much for the Oxen, who turned round indignantly and said, "Hullo, you there! Why do you make such a noise when we do all the work?" They complain most who suffer least.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what were the Oxen drawing along the highway?
According to the passage, what did the Axletrees do as the Oxen tugged and strained at the yoke?
According to the passage, how did the Oxen turn when they had had enough?
According to the passage, what do the Oxen ask the Axletrees?
options: Why they make such a noise when the Oxen do all the work
Why they never help pull the waggon
Why they were built so poorly
Why they need to be oiled so often

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what is stated as the moral at the end?
options: They complain most who suffer least
Heavy loads make the loudest noise
Silence is always a sign of strength

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "indignantly" mean in "turned round indignantly"?
Based on the passage, why do the Oxen find the Axletrees' complaint unfair?
options: The Axletrees never actually make any noise
The Oxen are doing the hard labor of pulling, while the Axletrees merely carry the load and yet complain loudly
The Axletrees are pulling more weight than the Oxen
The Oxen believe the Axletrees are lying about the waggon's weight

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Those who do the least work often complain the loudest
Waggons should be built without axletrees
Oxen are always stronger than the tools they pull
Complaining is the best way to get help with a heavy task

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where were the Oxen drawing the waggon?
According to the passage, what were the Oxen doing at the yoke as the Axletrees creaked?
According to the passage, what exact words do the Oxen use to get the Axletrees' attention?
As the passage uses it, what best describes the sound the Axletrees made?
Based on the passage, what does the Oxen's question suggest about who is really working hardest?
options: The Oxen believe they, not the Axletrees, bear the real burden of the task
The Oxen believe the Axletrees are working just as hard as they are
The Oxen believe the waggon itself is doing all the work
The Oxen believe the highway is to blame for the noise

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: The Axletrees pull the waggon while the Oxen creak and groan loudly
The Oxen ask the Axletrees to help pull the heavy waggon
The Oxen scold the creaking Axletrees for complaining loudly while doing none of the actual work
The Oxen and Axletrees agree to share the burden of the waggon equally
